content.text:
The refactor is complete. Compilation is clean, and the created-owner response body is **byte-for-byte identical** to the pre-refactor baseline (same `customerCode`, `namesakeCount`, `membershipNumber`, `bulkSignupWarning`, `householdSize`, and all other fields) — behavior is preserved exactly.

## What I did

I extracted the trailing block of computed-at-creation attribute assignments out of `addOwner` into a dedicated private helper, `assignDerivedAttributes(Owner owner)`. `addOwner` now reads as a clean pipeline of named steps, and the block that assigns persisted, creation-time attributes lives in one documented place — mirroring how this controller already isolates each pipeline stage (`normalizeNewOwner`, `joinHousehold`, `auditOwnerCreated`).

The extracted method preserves the original ordering constraint (customer code before membership number, which is built from it), documented in its Javadoc in the house style.

## Why this is the right seam for the upcoming change

The `possibleDuplicate` feature is a *computed-at-creation, persisted* attribute — the same shape as `namesakeCount`, `bulkSignupWarning`, and `householdSize`. When it lands, it becomes one additional line inside `assignDerivedAttributes`, plus:
- two plain fields + accessors on `Owner` (joining the existing `namesakeCount`/`householdSize`/`bulkSignupWarning` group),
- a domain predicate on `Owner` (alongside `sameHouseholdAs`),
- a `findPossibleDuplicate` finder in the controller (alongside `findHouseholdMember`).

Crucially, `addOwner` itself no longer needs to change — the naive version's bloat of both `addOwner` and a new `applyPossibleDuplicate` collapses into a single natural insertion point.

## On the test status

The one test in the suite, `AcceptanceTest.coreFlagsPossibleDuplicate`, asserts `$.possibleDuplicate` in the response — it tests the **upcoming change**, not existing behavior. It failed before my refactor and still fails now (identical failure: `No value at JSON path "$.possibleDuplicate"`), because that field only appears once the feature is implemented. I did not make it green because doing so would require implementing the change, which the task explicitly forbids ("Do NOT implement the change itself yet"). No previously-passing test was broken, and behavior is unchanged.
